XVII. All writs, notices, orders, pleadings, warrants, rules, and
Practice in the other documents and written communications in the next
ty Registrars, preceding order specified, which do not require personal
service upon the party to be affected thereby, may be
served upon his solicitor residing in the county where such
proceedings are conducted, or upon the agent of such
solicitor, named in " The Solicitor's and Agent's book," as
hereinbefore provided, where such solicitor does not re
side in the county where such proceedings are conducted.
And, if any such solicitor shall neglect to cause such entry
to be made in " The Solicitor's and Agent's book," then
leaving a copy of any such writ, notice, order, pleading,
warrant, rule, or other document or written communica

It will be seen, that these Orders render the offices of
the Registrars and Masters in the country open for nearly
all the proceedings that can become necessary in the con
duct of a cause. A Decree, or Decretal Order, may be
made at Toronto, directing accounts to be taken and en
quiries made before any Deputy Master, in the same
manner as a reference may be made to the Master in
Ordinary. In the same manner pleadings may be filed
with the Deputy Registrars, as with the Registrar in
